subject: general
question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tall building from the points M and N at the distances of 72 m and 128 m, respectilvely, from the base of the building and in the same straight line with it, are complementary. The height of the building (in m) is:
solution:
**Given:**

The distance of point M from the building = 72 m

The distance of point N from the building = 128 m

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21f226da8ab9f064893a9c4bebe477bf98c07d259685f0fd113d75a052a84ed3.png] 

Here, ∠BNA and ∠BMA are complementary

Let, ∠BMA = θ

So, ∠BNA = (90° - θ)

Suppose, the height of the building (AB) = x m

In ΔBMA, tan θ = AB/AM

⇒ tan θ = x/72 .....(1)

In ΔBNA, tan (90° - θ) = AB/AN

⇒ tan (90° - θ) = x/128

⇒ cot θ = x/128 [∵ tan (90° - θ) = cot θ]

⇒ tan θ = 128/x [∵ tan θ = 1/cot θ] .....(2)

So, x/72 = 128/x

⇒ x² = 72 × 128

⇒ x2 = 9216

⇒ x = √9216 = 96

**∴ The height of the building (in m) is 96 m**
